hed: UK defence chief: more than 500,000 Russian troops killed in Ukraine; 1.5 million casualties
dek: Air Chief Marshal Sir Richard Knighton, chief of the U.K. Defence Staff, said Friday that more than half a million Russian troops have been killed since Moscow's full-scale invasion began in February 2022, part of about 1.5 million total Russian casualties. British defence intelligence confirmed the 500,000 killed figure among Ukrainian General Staff tallies published midweek; Knighton said 1.4 million of the casualties came since January 2023 for about 2% of Ukrainian territory. He also cited more than 10,000 armored vehicles, nearly 3,000 air-defense and artillery systems, and over 370 aircraft and helicopters lost. There was no immediate comment from Russian officials. Neither Moscow nor Kyiv publishes regular battlefield death totals.

cl.body: The Los Angeles Times (AP), Local 10's AP wire, and India Today place Knighton's 500,000-killed / 1.5 million-casualty tally beside Friday's civilian gas-station and shopping-mall drone strikes in Kyiv and Pavlohrad, a slowed Russian advance, and Ukraine's long-range hits on Russian refineries — framing the milestone as the human cost of Putin's invasion as Moscow still struggles for territory.

cr.body: Forces News and the UK Defence Journal stress Knighton's math — 1.4 million casualties since January 2023 for roughly 2% of Ukraine, plus enormous kit losses — and his line that Britain will keep standing with Kyiv while Putin could end the war tomorrow; the New York Post's CSIS coverage of an 8-to-1 Russian-to-Ukrainian kill ratio casts the new 500,000-dead mark as confirmation that attrition still favors Ukraine if Western support holds.
